# A STUBBED upstream vLLM metric set — NOT a copy of the real one, and it must
# never be updated to track upstream.
#
# scripts/check-vllm-buckets.py --selftest matches a stubbed set of OUR names
# against this file to test its `_total` rule, which is the one piece of
# judgement in that script and the one that fails silently when it is wrong:
#
#   * a blanket `_total` strip reports "in sync" while a name we emit has no
#     upstream counterpart at all
#   * no strip at all reports drift on every counter we emit, every week, until
#     someone stops reading the output
#
# Neither shows up in the real run, which prints a plausible answer either way.
# A fixture is the only way to assert the rule, because the real upstream file
# is the moving thing this whole script exists to watch — testing against it
# would make the test drift with the very input it is meant to pin.
#
# Each name below is a CASE. Read the selftest beside it.

# Exactly as we emit it: matches directly.
vllm:num_requests_running

# Declared WITHOUT the suffix. The Prometheus client appends `_total` at
# exposition time, so our `vllm:prompt_tokens_total` is this metric.
vllm:prompt_tokens

# ⚠️ Declared WITH the suffix, and a histogram rather than a counter. Upstream's
# naming is not uniform, so this must match our `vllm:iteration_tokens_total`
# EXACTLY rather than being stripped to a `vllm:iteration_tokens` that upstream
# does not declare.
vllm:iteration_tokens_total

# Upstream declares these and the stubbed set does not emit them: a gap, listed
# clearly and exiting 0. Upstream adds metrics regularly, and reddening a weekly
# scheduled run for each one trains people to ignore it.
#
# Deliberately invented names. A real upstream metric here would read as a claim
# about what this repo does or does not emit, and would go stale the day someone
# closed that gap.
vllm:not_emitted_here
vllm:some_new_metric
